# Embassy v1.0.0

Embassy is a personal, local-only gateway that lets your running Claude Code sessions and Codex desktop tasks find each other by name and exchange messages — in both directions, on one machine, under your explicit control. It is a small alias router and bounded message broker, not an agent runtime: it never wraps, replaces, or re-implements either product, and `embassy serve` opens no network connection of its own (the opt-in `embassy dashboard --live` companion is the sole loopback listener — see "Live dashboard" below). “Local” describes the broker and route, not model inference: delivered text enters the receiving cloud-backed product as an ordinary model turn and is retained under that product's normal conversation policy.

**Headline capabilities**

- Bidirectional messaging with paired consent: registration makes one Codex task visible through Claude's native `ListAgents`/`SendMessage`, while selecting a Claude session makes it both the Codex destination and the only accepted inbound sender. Other senders settle with `SENDER_NOT_PAIRED`; `serve --inbound open` is the explicit opt-out.
- Queue-while-busy delivery — Embassy never interrupts or steers a turn to force a message through; it queues and dispatches automatically once the target goes idle.
- Conversation continuation via a returned token, from either side.
- A private, metadata-only static dashboard — `gateway-dashboard.html` plus its `gateway-dashboard.zh-CN.html` twin, cross-linked in the page — showing routes, states, and queue depth, never message content. A static page is a point-in-time snapshot and never refreshes itself.
- Opt-in live dashboard companion (`embassy dashboard --live`) — authenticated, read-only, loopback-bound, and a separate process from the broker.
- Normalized, bounded receipts — `delivered`, `unconfirmed`, `ambiguous`, `expired`, `failed`, `cancelled` — readable by delivery token through `delivery-status` and `wait-delivery`, plus a single safe diagnostic frame on failure, never a raw path, identifier, or exception.
- A repo-shipped agent skill so a Claude session or Codex task can drive the whole workflow without hand-paraphrased instructions.
- Hard version pins on both provider surfaces, with fail-closed behavior on any unrecognized version.

**Compatibility pins**

- Claude Code **2.1.225**, peer protocol 1 (still-running 2.1.224 sessions stay discoverable during a patch-upgrade overlap).
- Codex desktop app with managed standalone App Server **0.147.0**, resolved by exact path — a `codex` on `PATH` is not used.
- Node.js ≥ 20.
- macOS; the public v1 launcher does not support other operating systems.

**Retiring the MCP task lifecycle**

The one-way MCP task lifecycle (the six `claude_task_*` tools) existed only in the unpublished prototype. It was never released publicly and is not present in Embassy v1; the gateway is now the only product in this repo.

**Live dashboard**

New in this release: `embassy dashboard --live` adds an opt-in live dashboard companion, a separate foreground process that streams the same sanitized metadata as the static dashboard into a browser tab. It binds `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port; `embassy serve` itself remains socket-only with no TCP or HTTP listener. Access bootstraps through a one-use 256-bit token exchanged for a scoped session cookie, with the exact Host checked on every request (navigation GETs permit a missing Origin; non-navigation POSTs require exact Origin plus the X-Embassy-Request sentinel). The only mutations are explicitly confirmed select-Claude, unselect-Claude, and refresh-discovery actions, capped at 1 KiB and six per minute; there is no generic control, provider, CORS, storage, telemetry, or external-asset surface. Any process running as your OS user, including root and browser extensions with local access, can read what the browser can read. An optional `--lang en|zh-CN` flag selects the companion's display language; the static pair is always written in both languages and switched by an in-page link. The static `gateway-dashboard.html` and `gateway-dashboard.zh-CN.html` files remain the offline floor.

**Known limits**

- Exactly one registered Codex task at a time per gateway process. It is visible to every compatible live Claude session running as the same OS user, but paired mode accepts only the selected session. Handing the registration to another task requires `register-codex --succeeds`, which drains and retires the old route first and transfers nothing.
- macOS is the only platform supported by v1.
- Message bodies are memory-only in transit and are never persisted: if the broker exits, queued and in-flight messages are marked abandoned, their bodies discarded, and nothing is replayed — this is by design, not a bug to be fixed later.
- Single-user, same-machine software only: run it under an OS account that is yours alone, and never host, share, or expose it on a network.

Unofficial community project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or OpenAI.
